claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

is_adopting.description: Whether the claimant is adopting the child.

child_has_moved_in.description: Whether the child being adopted has come to live with the claimant.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions.

Let's start with: **Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have a child. I'm asking about my son Alex, who is 8 years old. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! You have an 8-year-old son named Alex. 

To help determine your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to ask you a few questions:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to understand your relationship with Alex:

**Are you responsible for Alex? For example, does he live with you, or are you paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit (or equivalent) towards looking after him - such as for food, clothes, or pocket money?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He doesn't live with me at the moment, but I do contribute towards his upkeep. I help out with money for his clothes, food, and other things he needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. It's important to understand the details of your contributions:

**How much do you contribute towards Alex's upkeep, and how often do you make these contributions (weekly, monthly, or as a lump sum)? Also, do you know the current Child Benefit rates - are your contributions at least equal to or more than what Child Benefit would pay?**

For reference, Child Benefit is currently paid at different rates depending on whether it's for the eldest/only child or additional children.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I contribute £30 a week towards Alex's upkeep - that's what I pay regularly to help with his needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that detail. Now I need to understand Alex's living situation a bit better:

**Who does Alex currently live with, and how long has he been living with them?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex lives with his mum. He's been living with her for quite a while now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. I need to clarify a few more things:

**Is Alex's mum currently claiming Child Benefit for him, or do you know if anyone else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, his mum isn't claiming Child Benefit for him, and no one else is claiming it either.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I have a few more questions to complete the assessment:

**How long has it been since Alex stopped living with you? Is it more or less than 8 weeks?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Actually, Alex hasn't lived with me yet. I'm in the process of adopting him, but he hasn't come to live with me yet.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that - this is important information. I need to understand your adoption situation better:

**Has Alex come to live with you yet as part of the adoption process, or is he still living with his mum and the adoption hasn't reached that stage yet?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's still living with his mum. The adoption process is ongoing, but he hasn't come to live with me yet.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. I need to understand the situation a bit better:

**What is your relationship to Alex and his mum? Are you adopting Alex from his mum, or is this a different arrangement? Also, is the local council paying anything towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance while he lives with his mum?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm adopting Alex, but he hasn't moved in with me yet. His mum is his current carer. The local council isn't paying anything towards his accommodation or maintenance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. To complete my assessment, I need to clarify one final point:

**Since you're in the process of adopting Alex but he hasn't come to live with you yet, and you're making financial contributions to his mum who he currently lives with - is his mum a relative or friend, or is this a formal fostering/care arrangement? Also, do you know if his mum is eligible to claim Child Benefit herself but is simply choosing not to?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: His mum could claim Child Benefit herself - she's eligible, she's just not claiming it at the moment. I'm contributing towards his upkeep while the adoption process goes through.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Let me carefully consider your situation based on the Child Benefit rules.

Based on what you've told me:

- Alex is 8 years old (under 16, so age-eligible)
- You live in the UK
- Alex does not live with you yet - he still lives with his mum
- You contribute £30 per week towards Alex's upkeep
- The adoption process is ongoing, but Alex hasn't come to live with you yet
- His mum is currently his carer and is eligible to claim Child Benefit but isn't claiming it
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex

According to the Child Benefit rules, you can claim Child Benefit for a child you're adopting **as soon as the child comes to live with you** - you don't have to wait until the adoption process is complete. However, the key requirement is that the child must have come to live with you.

Since Alex has not yet come to live with you and is still living with his mum (who is his current carer), you would not be eligible to claim Child Benefit for him at this time. The rules state you're normally responsible for a child if you live with them OR you're paying towards their upkeep - but in this case, his mum is the person he lives with and she would be the person entitled to claim Child Benefit.

Once Alex comes to live with you as part of the adoption process, you will be able to claim Child Benefit for him at that point.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: **Summary:** You are currently **not eligible** to claim Child Benefit for Alex at this time. However, you will be able to claim Child Benefit as soon as Alex comes to live with you as part of the adoption process - you won't need to wait for the adoption to be fully completed, just for him to move in with you.
